coverage_notes: Every supplied observation and CSV row was reviewed. Every registered anchor page, including secondary locations, was actually viewed. This is alignment of the exact supplied registry, not a full-paper census or proof of the source presentation used by the original curators. All inputs are unchanged.
shared_qualifications: Critical pitting Ec is explicitly the rapid anodic-current rise associated with breakdown and actively growing pits (PDF p.3). All potentials here use SCE; no reference offset is applied.

C1: explicitly identified monovalent NaCl and HCl each supply one chloride equivalent per mole. Thus 1 N NaCl gives 1 mol/L chloride; 1 N NaCl +0.5 N HCl gives 1.5 mol/L chloride. This species-specific relation is not a generic normality conversion and does not infer pH.

C2: the neutral 30 C scan is 20 mV/min =20/60=0.333333 mV/s. The more aggressive acid tests instead use 6 mV/min =0.1 mV/s (PDF p.2), conflicting with CRA 0.3333 for Nos.246-252. Source Table 3 footnote specifies acid conditions 50 C, pH0.69. Neutral-solution pH7.0 is not independently established in the inspected source.

CRA245 has CL- [M]=1.5 for its neutral 1 N NaCl result; the source implies 1 mol/L, retained as a conflict. Table 1 estimates (~) and upper limits (<) are not exact composition values; in particular approximate nickel contents are preserved below. Missing Mn for alloy27 is not treated as zero.

obs_021 retains the no-breakdown limit 708 mV in Table 2 and 908 mV in its Table 3 repetition. Neither is replaced by an observed threshold. Table 3 parenthesized values are current densities, not potentials. The separate Figure 1 bounds/onset at 70 C are not the 50 C acid condition.
